SUTF framing

The SuperUnicode Character Encoding Forms: SUTF-8, SUTF-16, SUTF-4, SUTF-2 and vSUTF.

Form Code unit Covers Shape
SUTF-8 byte Full 31-bit space Default stream encoding; variable, 1–6 bytes. UTF-8 parity to 0x10FFFF, extending to 6 bytes for the native extended planes.
SUTF-16 16-bit word Full 31-bit space 1–2 words: one to 0x7FFF, two above. No surrogates — 0xD800–0xDFFF are valid PUA. Endian-neutral; byte order is decided by the SUST transport.
SUTF-4 4-bit nibble Full 31-bit space Fixed 8 nibbles (4 bytes) per codepoint; console dumps, terminal logging and bus debugging.
SUTF-2 2-bit frame Full 31-bit space Fixed 16 frames (4 bytes) per codepoint; compressed framing for narrow inter-thread IPC.
vSUTF byte Full 64-bit ExtSUCS space Variable streaming form with a Base-SUCS fast path.

Reference implementations live in modules/sutf (Level 3 forms) and modules/sust (Level 4 serialization, SUST-16 big-endian canonical plus the fixed SUST-32/64/128/256/512/N widths); the framing tables are published at Public/0.1.0/sutf/. Extended codepoints use vector, vsutf and e-SUST. For why forms and transports are separate levels, see SUTR-7.
